To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the BLSTM-RNN is a powerful tool for noise robustness, and that the integration of information from BLSTM-RNN and HMM is best done in a Dynamic Bayesian Network.
a hybrid system based on a Dynamic Belief Network and a BLSTM-RNN is able to improve noise robust ASR.
the use of a BLSTM-RNN as an additional observation model in a DBN improves robustness in noise, and the integration of the complete BLSTM output in the DBN further improves robustness.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the hybrid HMM/BLSTMRNN is the state of the art in noise robust ASR, and that the BLSTMRNN is a powerful tool for noise robustness.
there is no single best approach to combine HMMs and BLSTM-RNNs for noise-robust ASR.
the integration of BLSTM-RNN into the DBN is beneficial for robust speech recognition.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the BLSTM-RNN provides a powerful tool to integrate long-range context information into a speech decoding scheme, and that the hybrid DBN/BLSTM-RNNS system is a very promising approach for noise robust AS.

a hybrid system is able to combine the advantages of HMMs (robustness to noise) with the benefits of BLSTM-RNNs (long-range context information) and that a DBN is a promising framework for such a combination.
the BLSTM-RNN can be seen as a very good feature extractor.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the BLSTM-RNN is able to provide useful evidence for the DBN, which is not only based on the phoneme identity but also on the probability of each phoneme candidate.
the BLSTM-RNN provides a very good feature representation for ASR, and that the DBN provides an optimal way to integrate this representation into an existing speech recognition system.
it is possible to integrate the output of a neural network in a speech recognition system without losing the advantages of HMMs.
